title: Close enough?
description: Decide whether a guess is close or out of range by joining comparisons together.

tasks.title: Join two questions into one
tasks.body: and, or and not combine True and False. A and B is True only when both are True. A or B is True when at least one of them is True. not flips True to False, and False to True.
tasks.detail: Each side of and or or is a whole comparison: write x > 0 and x < 10, not x > 0 and < 10. Python works out the comparisons first, then not, then and, then or. Use parentheses when you want to be sure of the order.

tasks.code:
# The bridge is safe for 2 to 6 travellers
travellers = 7
print(travellers >= 2 and travellers <= 6)
# Too few or too many?
print(travellers < 2 or travellers > 6)
# Flip the first answer with not
print(not (travellers >= 2 and travellers <= 6))
tasks.note: 7 is at least 2 but more than 6, so the and line is False. The or line needs only one side to be True, and 7 > 6 is. not flips the first answer from False to True.

tasks.question: If travellers were 2, what would the first print() show?
tasks.why: 2 >= 2 is True and 2 <= 6 is True. With and, both sides are True, so the whole line is True.

tasks.prompt: Try travellers = 2, then 6, then 0, and predict the three lines before each run. Then change and to or in the first print(). Find a number of travellers where the answer changes, and explain why.

The riddle keeper's secret number is always from 1 to 100. Ask for the secret and the guess, as whole numbers. Print three lines, each True or False: is the guess close (no more than 2 away from the secret, on either side); is the guess out of range (below 1 or above 100); and is the guess not close? Print just the three answers.
tasks.starter:
# Ask for the secret number, then the guess, as whole numbers
# Print True or False: close, out of range, not close
hints: Three lines, three joined questions. Close needs two comparisons joined with and. Out of range needs two joined with or. The last line flips the first one with not.
Close means the guess is at least secret - 2 and at most secret + 2. Out of range means below 1 or above 100. Check whether each limit should use < or <=.
A pattern with other names: print(depth >= low and depth <= high) checks that depth sits between two limits. Putting not ( ) around a question flips its answer.

error_hints.text: Each side of and and or needs a whole comparison, like guess >= 1 and guess <= 100. Writing guess >= 1 and <= 100 makes Python stop.
Give secret and guess their values from input() before you compare them, and spell them the same each time.
A guess of 53 is 3 away from 50, so it is not close. If your first line says True, check whether you joined the two limits with or: or is True when either side is, and here one side always is.
52 is exactly 2 away from 50, which still counts as close. Check that your limits use <= and >=, so the edge is included.
0 is below 1, so it is out of range: True. Out of range needs or, because a guess can't be below 1 and above 100 at the same time.
Check both ends of the range: a guess equal to the highest or lowest allowed answer is still in range.
A guess equal to the lowest allowed answer is still in range, and a guess 1 away from the secret is close. Check each < against <=.

similar_example.code:
temperature = 18
print(temperature >= 15 and temperature <= 25)
print(not temperature > 30)
similar_example.note: 18 is between 15 and 25, so the first line is True, and 18 is not over 30, so the second line is True too. Your challenge checks a guess against limits that come from the secret number.

other_ways.code:
secret = int(input("Secret number? "))
guess = int(input("Your guess? "))
close = secret - 2 <= guess <= secret + 2
print(close)
print(guess < 1 or guess > 100)
print(not close)
other_ways.note: Python lets you chain two comparisons, which reads like maths: low <= x <= high.

other_ways.code:
secret = int(input("Secret number? "))
guess = int(input("Your guess? "))
distance = guess - secret
close = distance >= -2 and distance <= 2
print(close)
print(not (1 <= guess <= 100))
print(not close)
other_ways.note: Work out how far away the guess is first. Out of range is the same as not in range.
